page: Microsoft Azure D2ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DADSv5 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The instance features 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core via Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor virtualization. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the server includes a bundled 77 GB SSD and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is strong, ranking in the top 25% with a score of 2701.89. However, multi-core performance is weak, falling into the bottom 25% with the same score of 2701.89. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck; the passmark memory score and read-only small block memory bandwidth both rank in the bottom 10%. Similarly, database operations and Redis SET operations perform poorly, placing in the bottom 10%. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show average performance in the middle 50%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D2ads_v5 offers a low-cost entry point for dedicated AMD EPYC resources with bundled local SSD storage. However, the resource density and memory bandwidth limitations present clear tradeoffs for resource-intensive applications. This server is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, single-threaded processing tasks, or development and testing environments that do not require high multi-threaded throughput or intensive database operations.
